note: What a server sends to place a prop on the map: a thing that stands there and is looked at rather than one that acts. The header carries zero or names the object this is about, and a client accepts either.

fields.name: prop
fields.note: The name the prop answers to, so later messages can name it.

fields.name: node
fields.note: Which network node the object belongs to. It is a field of its own, not the leading byte of the name beside it.

fields.name: atX
fields.note: Where the prop stands, along one ground axis, in world units.

fields.name: atY
fields.note: Where the prop stands, in height, in world units.

fields.name: atZ
fields.note: Where the prop stands, along the other ground axis, in world units.

fields.name: firstX
fields.note: A vector's part along one ground axis, used for either kind. What this carries is not recorded.

fields.name: firstY
fields.note: A vector's part in height, used for either kind. What this carries is not recorded.

fields.name: firstZ
fields.note: A vector's part along the other ground axis, used for either kind. What this carries is not recorded.

fields.name: secondX
fields.note: A second vector's part along one ground axis, used only where kind is 1. What this carries is not recorded.

fields.name: secondY
fields.note: A second vector's part in height, used only where kind is 1. What this carries is not recorded.

fields.name: secondZ
fields.note: A second vector's part along the other ground axis, used only where kind is 1. What this carries is not recorded.

fields.name: side
fields.note: The side the prop belongs to.

bits.name: unused
bits.note: A client reads nothing here; a server sends zero.

fields.name: unused
fields.note: A client reads nothing here; a server sends zero.

fields.name: skillLevel
fields.note: Used only where kind is 0. What this carries is not recorded.

fields.name: kind
fields.note: What sort of prop it is; a client makes nothing for any other value.

1.name: attached
1.note: A prop attached to the object named in name.

fields.name: name
fields.note: What this prop is called, so a client can tell one from another. Written out in full and padded with zero bytes to the width above.

fields.name: asset
fields.note: The name of the character the client loads the prop's art and sound under, written and padded as above. A client given one it lacks fails soon after, once the prop is near what it draws.

fields.name: prop
fields.note: The name the prop answers to, so later messages can name it.

fields.name: node
fields.note: Which network node the object belongs to. It is a field of its own, not the leading byte of the name beside it.

fields.name: skin
fields.note: Which look the prop wears.

fields.name: atX
fields.note: Where the prop stands, along one ground axis, in world units.

fields.name: atY
fields.note: Where the prop stands, in height, in world units.

fields.name: atZ
fields.note: Where the prop stands, along the other ground axis, in world units.

fields.name: rotationX
fields.note: For scenery, the pitch in degrees: a turn about the x axis, positive turning +y toward +z. For an active prop, x of the direction it faces.

fields.name: rotationY
fields.note: For scenery, the yaw in degrees: a turn about the up axis, positive turning +z toward +x, so yaw 0 faces +z and 90 faces +x. For an active prop, y of its facing, which does not turn it.

fields.name: rotationZ
fields.note: For scenery, the roll in degrees: a turn about the z axis, positive turning +x toward +y. For an active prop, z of the direction it faces.

fields.name: offsetX
fields.note: What is added to where it stands, along one ground axis, in world units.

fields.name: offsetY
fields.note: What is added to where it stands, in height, in world units.

fields.name: offsetZ
fields.note: What is added to where it stands, along the other ground axis, in world units.

fields.name: scaleX
fields.note: What its drawn size is scaled by, along one ground axis.

fields.name: scaleY
fields.note: What its drawn size is scaled by, in height.

fields.name: scaleZ
fields.note: What its drawn size is scaled by, along the other ground axis.

fields.name: side
fields.note: The side the prop belongs to. A server sends 300, the neutral side.

fields.name: skillLevel
fields.note: Unused; a server writes zero.

fields.name: rank
fields.note: How far it is advanced.

fields.name: kind
fields.note: What sort of prop it is; a client makes nothing for any other value. A client first deletes any object holding the prop's id, whatever the kind.

0.name: active
0.note: Uses name, asset, skin, side, position, the three rotations and rank; not offset or scale.

1.name: scenery
1.note: Uses name, asset, skin, position, rotation (pitch, yaw, roll in degrees), offset and scale; not side or rank. Where the map has a placement point of the same name, its position is used instead; where a scenery prop of that name already stands there, it is reused and takes the new id.

fields.name: name
fields.note: What this prop is called, so a client can tell one from another. Written out in full and padded with zero bytes to the width above.

fields.name: asset
fields.note: The name the client loads its art and sound under, written and padded as above.

revisions.note: A client takes the prop's id from prop, not from the header. A scenery prop is turned by pitch, then yaw, then roll, each about the fixed world axes; none is negated or wrapped. An active prop only turns about the up axis, to face the ground direction its x and z give, and faces +z where both are zero.
